svg.title: c.1895 Aseptic Operating Theatre: Anaesthesia + Germ-Free Environment
svg.desc: Architectural cross-section of a late-Victorian c.1895 aseptic operating theatre registered to the 1840 room geometry: specialist anaesthetist administering regulated chloroform/ether inhaler, steam autoclave steriliser, surgeons in boiled white gowns, caps, masks, and Halsted rubber gloves, washable tiled walls and floor, and a sealed glass viewing screen, cutting post-operative sepsis mortality under 5%.
svg.text: EDEXCEL GCSE HISTORY · LATE VICTORIAN SURGICAL REVOLUTION (ASEPSIS)
c.1895 Aseptic Operating Theatre: Anaesthesia + Germ-Free Environment
SEALED STEEL-AND-GLASS SKYLIGHT + FILTERED VENTILATION & ELECTRIC LIGHT

g.text: a dedicated anaesthetist keeps the patient
still for slow, intricate internal surgery.
scrubbed hands, boiled white gowns, caps,
Zero breath or street dust enters theatre

svg.text: TWO OF THREE BARRIERS CONQUERED BY 1895: PAIN (ANAESTHESIA) + INFECTION (ANTISEPTIC → ASEPTIC SURGERY)
Pasteur's Germ Theory (1861) & Lister's Carbolic Acid (1867) evolved into 1890s germ-free asepsis; safe blood transfusions followed Landsteiner's 1901 ABO groups.
Excluded microbes before they could ever reach the surgical incision
Surgeons safely opened the abdomen (appendicectomy, 1880s) and joints;
only major blood loss remained unsolved until 1901 ABO groups & WWI storage.
